discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald developed a continuum theory of twisted bilayer graphene and predicted that, at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac velocity vanishes and nearly flat bands form, where electron-electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realised this regime experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene. This rare union of a precise theoretical prediction with a decisive experiment created 'twistronics': the twist angle became a new tuning knob for quantum matter. Moire materials now host orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, strange-metal behaviour and, in twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. The work opened a major, highly tunable platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electrons, and it is changing how condensed-matter physicists design quantum materials.
